title: Good News for Drivers: Fuel Tax Cut Extended Until End of Year!
summary: If your family drives a car, here's some good news: the government says it will keep the 5p cut on fuel duty until the end of the year! Fuel duty is a tax added to petrol and diesel. In 2022, after Russia invaded Ukraine and prices shot up, the government cut this tax by 5 pence per litre. It was supposed to end, but it's been extended again and again. Now, Prime Minister Keir Starmer says it will stay until December 2026 because of the war in Iran, which has made global oil supplies tight. On Monday, the average price of petrol hit 158.52p per litre — the highest since the Iran war started. Starmer told Parliament, "We're backing drivers by extending the freeze on fuel duty." He also announced a bigger cut on red diesel, which farmers use in tractors, and a one-year holiday on vehicle tax for heavy goods vehicles (HGVs) to help the haulage industry. But not everyone is cheering. The RAC, a drivers' group, wonders what will happen next year. Will the full 5p come back all at once? The Conservative Party says the government made a "U-turn" because they had called for this freeze earlier. They say Labour's plan would have hurt families and businesses. Still, for now, filling up the car will be a little less painful. How does this affect your family's budget? Every penny counts!
why_it_matters: When fuel costs go up, everything from school trips to food prices can get more expensive, so this tax cut helps families keep more money for other things.

background_read: Fuel duty is like a hidden tax that drivers pay every time they fill up their tank, and it makes up a big chunk of the price.
Keir Starmer is the UK's Prime Minister, and he leads the Labour Party, which is in charge right now.
The RAC is an organisation that gives advice and breakdown help to drivers, and it speaks up for motorists when taxes rise.
Article_Structure: WHO: Prime Minister Keir Starmer and the UK government, as well as drivers and businesses.
WHAT: The government extended the 5p cut on fuel duty until December 2026, and also cut tax on red diesel and gave a holiday on vehicle tax for HGVs.
WHERE: The announcement was made in Parliament, affecting all of the United Kingdom.
WHY: Due to the war in Iran causing tight oil supplies and high petrol prices, the government aimed to help families and the haulage industry save money.

perspectives.description: They believe extending the cut is the right thing to do to support families struggling with high petrol prices caused by a war.
They are happy for now, but they're anxious that the full tax could suddenly return in 2027, which would shock motorists.
They say the government made a U-turn because they previously planned to end the cut, and now they're only doing what the Tories suggested.
